examples.ko: 안 쓰는 물건을 그냥 내다버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just throw out things you don't use.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 오래된 가구를 다 내다버렸어요.
examples.en: I threw out all the old furniture before moving.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 길에 내다버리는 사람이 아직도 있어요.
examples.en: There are still people who dump their trash on the street.

examples.ko: 이 낡은 소파는 언제 내다버릴 거예요?
examples.en: When are you going to throw out this worn-out sofa?
I'm throwing out the broken umbrella now.

examples.ko: 아까워서 내다버리지 못하고 창고에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: It seemed a waste, so I couldn't throw it out and put it in the storage room.

explain: '버리다'와 달리 집 안에 있던 것을 밖으로 들고 나가서 버리는 동작이 느껴져요. 쓸모없어진 가구나 물건에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '버리다', it suggests carrying something from inside the house out to throw it away. It fits well with furniture and things that are no longer useful.

examples.en: You can see the sea from my window.
The garden was clearly visible through the living room window.
This room is high up, so you can see far out.

examples.ko: 커튼을 열면 시장 골목이 내다보이는 집이에요.
examples.en: It's a house where you can see the market alley when you open the curtain.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 밖이 잘 내다보이지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of the fog, I can't see outside well.

examples.ko: 옥상에 올라가면 동네가 다 내다보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you go up to the rooftop, you'll be able to see the whole neighborhood.

explain: 그냥 '보이다'와 달리 창문이나 문처럼 안쪽에서 바깥이 눈에 들어올 때 써요. 장소가 주어가 되어서 '이 방에서는 바다가 내다보여요'처럼 말해요. 보는 사람이 주어이면 '내다보다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '보이다', it is used when the outside comes into view from the inside, such as through a window or door. A place often serves as the subject, as in '이 방에서는 바다가 내다보여요'. When the person is the subject, use '내다보다'.

examples.en: When the light changed, the cars dashed forward.
The child sees their mom and runs with all their might.
I ran flat out to the bus stop so I wouldn't miss the bus.

examples.ko: 말이 들판을 시원하게 내달리는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The sight of the horse racing across the field was wonderful.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 우승을 향해 쉬지 않고 내달리고 있어요.
examples.en: That team is racing toward the championship without a break.

examples.ko: 종이 울리자마자 학생들이 교문 밖으로 내달려요.
examples.en: As soon as the bell rings, the students dash out of the school gate.

explain: '달리다'보다 힘차게 앞으로 뛰쳐나가는 느낌이 강해요. 사람, 말, 차에 두루 쓰고 '목표를 향해 내달리다'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It feels more energetic than '달리다', like bursting forward at speed. It is used for people, horses and cars, and also figuratively, as in '목표를 향해 내달리다'.

examples.ko: 화가 난 형이 가방을 바닥에 내동댕이쳤어요.
examples.en: My angry older brother flung his bag onto the floor.
The child hurls the toy into the corner of the room.
If you fling things like that, they'll break.
He tossed aside his long-held plan overnight.
Even if you're angry, please don't throw your phone down.

examples.ko: 동생이 신발을 현관에 내동댕이쳐 놓고 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling flung their shoes down in the entryway and left.

explain: '던지다'보다 홱 거칠게 던지는 느낌이고, 화가 났거나 물건을 함부로 다룰 때 잘 어울려요. 계획이나 책임을 아무렇게나 버린다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is rougher than '던지다', a sudden rough fling, and fits when someone is angry or careless with things. It is also used figuratively for casually discarding a plan or responsibility.

examples.en: The baby took a first step.
On a snowy road you have to step carefully.
Today I took the first step of a new life.

examples.ko: 무서워서 앞으로 한 발도 내디딜 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that I couldn't take even one step forward.

examples.ko: 한 발 더 내디디면 물에 빠져요.
examples.en: If you take one more step, you'll fall into the water.
They are new employees taking their first steps into society.

explain: '첫발을 내디디다'처럼 새로운 일의 시작을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '내딛다'(내딛어요)라고도 해요. 활용은 '내디뎌요, 내디뎠어요'로 줄어요.
explain_en: It often appears in '첫발을 내디디다', meaning to start something new. It can be shortened to '내딛다' (내딛어요). The conjugation contracts to '내디뎌요' and '내디뎠어요'.

examples.en: I hit the nail hard with a hammer.

examples.ko: 화가 난 듯 책상을 주먹으로 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: As if angry, he pounded the desk with his fist.
I was startled by the sound of lightning striking down.

examples.ko: 선생님이 화가 나서 칠판을 손으로 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: The teacher got angry and slammed the blackboard with their hand.
Be careful when you bring the axe down on firewood.

examples.ko: 선수가 공을 위에서 아래로 세게 내려쳤어요.
examples.en: The player smashed the ball hard from above.

explain: 그냥 '치다'와 달리 위에서 아래로 힘껏 때리는 방향이 분명해요. 망치나 주먹뿐 아니라 번개가 떨어질 때도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '치다', the downward direction of the blow is clear. It is used for hammers and fists, and also for lightning striking down.

examples.ko: 내리막길에서 브레이크를 세게 밟았더니 차가 끼익 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: When I hit the brakes hard on the downhill road, the car screeched.

examples.ko: 이 산업은 십 년 전에 이미 정점을 지나 내리막길에 들어섰어요.
examples.en: This industry passed its peak ten years ago and is already on the decline.
Slow your bike down on downhill stretches.
The street in front of my house slopes downhill, so it's slippery in winter.
Going up is hard, but the way down is quick.

examples.ko: 요즘 그 가수는 인기가 내리막을 걷고 있어요.
examples.en: These days that singer's popularity is on the decline.

explain: 반대말은 '오르막'이에요. 길뿐 아니라 인기나 경기가 나빠지는 때를 '내리막길을 걷다'처럼 비유로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 년째 내리막길을 걷고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company has been in decline for several years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 길이 아니라 인기, 실적, 건강이 점점 나빠지는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not refer to an actual road but to popularity, performance or health steadily getting worse.

explain_en: The opposite is '오르막' (uphill). Besides roads, it is used figuratively for a time when popularity or the economy is getting worse, as in '내리막길을 걷다'.

examples.en: House prices are trending down these days.
The exchange rate has been falling for the third day.
I'm glad gas prices have turned downward.
Stock prices are falling, so investing feels scary.
The news said prices have entered a downward trend.
This month's sales show a clear downward trend.

explain: 반대말은 '오름세'예요. 가격, 주가, 기온처럼 숫자가 변하는 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, '내림세로 돌아서다', '내림세에 접어들다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '오름세' (upward trend). It appears a lot in news about numbers such as prices, stocks and temperatures, in phrases like '내림세로 돌아서다' and '내림세에 접어들다'.

examples.ko: 회사 내부적 문제라서 밖에 말하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's an internal company matter, so it's hard to tell outsiders.
Internal conflict is growing bit by bit.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 내부적 해결이 먼저 필요해요.
examples.en: For this matter, an internal solution is needed first.
I hear a decision has already been made internally.

examples.ko: 내부적으로 의견이 나뉘어서 결론을 못 냈어요.
examples.en: Opinions were divided internally, so we couldn't reach a conclusion.
We set new internal rules for the team.

explain: 반대말은 '외부적'이에요. 말할 때는 '내부적으로'나 '내부적인'의 꼴로도 많이 쓰고, 회사나 단체의 '안쪽 사정'을 말할 때 잘 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '외부적' (external). In speech it is also often used as '내부적으로' or '내부적인', and it comes up when talking about the inside affairs of a company or group.

examples.ko: 저희 아버지는 힘든 내색 없이 묵묵히 가족을 위해 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My father worked quietly for the family without showing any sign of hardship.

examples.ko: 속상해도 친구 앞에서는 내색을 안 했어요.
examples.en: I was upset, but I didn't show it in front of my friend.

examples.ko: 그는 화난 내색도 하지 않고 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He didn't show any sign of anger and just smiled.
I tried hard not to show it even though I was sad.
Please don't show that you dislike it.

examples.ko: 동생은 아픈데도 아무 내색 없이 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went to school without letting on at all that they were sick.

explain: '내색을 하다', '내색 없이'처럼 쓰고, 대부분 '내색하지 않다'의 부정 표현으로 나와요. 속마음이 얼굴이나 행동에 드러나는 것을 말하며, 구어에서는 '티를 내다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used in '내색을 하다' and '내색 없이', and mostly appears in the negative, '내색하지 않다'. It is about inner feelings showing on your face or in your behavior. In casual speech people also say '티를 내다'.

examples.ko: 내숭 떨지 말고 그냥 배고프다고 말해요.
examples.en: Stop playing coy and just say you're hungry.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 처음 만난 사람 앞에서는 내숭을 떨어요.
examples.en: That friend acts coy in front of people they've just met.
They're so coy that it's hard to know what they really think.

examples.ko: 이제 내숭 그만 떨고 편하게 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop being coy now and eat comfortably.

examples.ko: 겉으로는 착해 보여도 알고 보면 내숭 덩어리예요.
examples.en: They look nice on the surface, but actually they're full of pretense.

examples.ko: 너 사실은 말 많은 거 알아, 내숭 부리지 마요.
examples.en: I know you actually talk a lot, so don't act coy.

explain: '내숭을 떨다', '내숭을 부리다'로 자주 말해요. 얌전하거나 모르는 척하며 속마음을 감추는 모습인데, 친한 사이에서 놀리듯 말하는 경우가 많아서 어른께는 조심해서 써야 해요.
explain_en: It is often said as '내숭을 떨다' or '내숭을 부리다'. It describes acting demure or innocent while hiding one's real nature. It is mostly used to tease close friends, so be careful using it with elders.

en: be forced out; be driven out; be expelled

examples.ko: 그는 집세를 못 내서 집에서 내쫓겼어요.
examples.en: He couldn't pay the rent and was kicked out of his house.
The stray cat keeps getting chased away from in front of the shop.
I'm anxious that I might be pushed out of the company.
I broke a promise and ended up being kicked out of the group.
I ended up in a situation of being thrown out by the owner.
I was suddenly thrown out and had nowhere to go.

explain: '내쫓다'(몰아내다)의 피동이에요. '집에서 내쫓기다'처럼 장소는 '-에서', 내쫓은 사람은 '-에게'로 말해요. '쫓겨나다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '내쫓다' (to drive out). The place takes '-에서' and the person who drove you out takes '-에게', as in '집에서 내쫓기다'. '쫓겨나다' is used with a similar meaning.

examples.en: I ignored my homework and only played games.
You can't abandon your responsibility and run away.
The child flung their bag down in the entryway and left it.
Word got around that he's someone who abandoned his family.
They do half the work and then just drop it.
Don't blow off your promise to a friend.

explain: 물건을 홱 던져 버린다는 뜻도 있지만, 일, 책임, 사람을 돌보지 않고 저버릴 때 더 많이 써요. 물리적으로 거칠게 던지는 동작은 '내동댕이치다'가 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It can mean flinging something away, but it is used more for abandoning work, responsibility or people without caring for them. For a rough physical throw, '내동댕이치다' fits better.

examples.ko: 저는 내향적 성격이라 모임이 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have an introverted personality, so gatherings are a bit tiring.

examples.ko: 내향적인 사람도 친구를 잘 사귈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Introverted people can make friends well too.
I'm introverted, so I need time alone.
My younger sibling is introverted but very warm inside.

examples.ko: 내향적 사람들은 소규모 모임을 좋아하는 편이에요.
examples.en: Introverted people tend to like small gatherings.
They look introverted, but once you get close they talk a lot.

explain: 반대말은 '외향적'이에요. 성격 이야기나 성격 유형 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '내성적'도 비슷하게 써요. '내향적인 성격'처럼 '-인'을 붙이거나 '내향적이다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '외향적' (extroverted). It comes up often when talking about personality or personality types, and '내성적' is used similarly. You can say '내향적인 성격' with '-인', or '내향적이다'.

en: water of a stream; water of a brook

examples.en: Children are splashing around in the clear stream.
It rained, so the stream swelled a lot.
Hearing the sound of a stream calms my mind.
In summer we play with our feet in the stream.
I walked up along the stream for a good while.
This stream doesn't dry up even in winter.

explain: '시냇물'이라고도 해요. 강보다 작고 졸졸 흐르는 물을 떠올리면 돼요. 비슷한 말로 '개울'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is also called '시냇물'. Think of a small, trickling flow of water, smaller than a river. A similar word is '개울'.

examples.en: The heating and cooling in this building work very well.

examples.ko: 사무실 냉난방 비용이 너무 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The office heating and cooling costs are too high.
I bought an air conditioner that can both cool and heat.

examples.ko: 도서관은 냉난방이 완비돼 있어서 공부하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The library is fully equipped with heating and cooling, so it's good for studying.

examples.ko: 냉난방을 줄이면 전기 요금을 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cut back on heating and cooling, you can save on electricity.

examples.ko: 이 집은 월세에 냉난방비가 포함돼 있어요.
examples.en: In this house, the monthly rent includes heating and cooling costs.

explain: 여름의 냉방과 겨울의 난방을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요. 부동산 광고나 건물 안내에서 '냉난방 시설'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It covers summer cooling and winter heating in a single word. You often see it in real estate ads and building information, as in '냉난방 시설'.

examples.en: Put the leftover meat in the freezer.

examples.ko: 냉동고가 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The freezer is full, so I can't put in any more.
The freezer door was open and the ice cream melted.
We brought a big new freezer into the shop.
Please take some ice out of the freezer.

examples.ko: 냉동고 속 만두가 벌써 석 달 됐어요.
examples.en: The dumplings in the freezer have been there three months already.

explain: 냉장고 안의 칸은 '냉동실'이라고 하고, 따로 서 있는 큰 냉동 기계나 가게용은 '냉동고'라고 해요. 반대로 차갑지만 얼리지 않는 칸은 '냉장실'이에요.
explain_en: The compartment inside a refrigerator is called '냉동실', while a separate standing freezer or a shop freezer is '냉동고'. The compartment that is cold but doesn't freeze is '냉장실'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 에어컨 바람을 쐬었더니 냉방병에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: After being in the air conditioning all day, I came down with air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병 때문에 머리가 아프고 몸이 으슬으슬해요.
examples.en: Because of air-conditioning sickness, I have a headache and the chills.
Lots of people get air-conditioning sickness in the office.

examples.ko: 냉방병을 막으려면 실내 온도를 너무 낮추지 마세요.
examples.en: To prevent air-conditioning sickness, don't set the room temperature too low.

examples.ko: 여름 감기가 사실은 냉방병일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: What seems like a summer cold could actually be air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병에 걸리지 않게 얇은 겉옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I brought a thin jacket so I wouldn't get air-conditioning sickness.

explain: 더운 바깥과 시원한 실내의 온도 차이 때문에 감기처럼 몸이 안 좋을 때 써요. 보통 '냉방병에 걸리다'라고 말해요. 여름에 자주 듣는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to feeling unwell, like a cold, because of the temperature gap between the hot outdoors and the cool indoors. People usually say '냉방병에 걸리다'. It is a word you hear a lot in summer.

examples.en: When you sprain your ankle, start with a cold compress.

examples.ko: 부은 곳에 냉찜질을 해 주니 좀 나아졌어요.
examples.en: Putting a cold compress on the swollen spot made it a little better.

examples.ko: 냉찜질은 하루에 몇 번 해야 해요?
examples.en: How many times a day should I use a cold compress?
I used an ice pack on it for about twenty minutes.
They say a cold compress is good right after an injury.

examples.ko: 열이 날 때 이마에 냉찜질을 해 줬어요.
examples.en: When the fever came, I put a cold compress on their forehead.

explain: 차가운 얼음주머니나 수건을 몸에 대는 것을 말해요. 반대로 따뜻하게 하는 것은 '온찜질'이에요. '냉찜질을 하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means holding a cold ice pack or towel against the body. The warm version is '온찜질'. You say '냉찜질을 하다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 너도나도 그 사업에 달려들고 있어요.
examples.en: These days young people are all jumping into that business.

examples.ko: 신제품이 나오자 사람들이 너도나도 사려고 했어요.
examples.en: When the new product came out, everyone wanted to buy it.
Everybody is talking only about stocks.
In the classroom, the students all raised their hands.
It's moving season, so everyone is going around looking at houses.
The students all took part in the volunteer work.

explain: '모두'와 달리 서로서로 따라 하며 한꺼번에 몰리는 분위기를 보여 줘요. 유행이나 인기, 몰려드는 상황에서 잘 쓰고 뒤에는 보통 동작이 와요.
explain_en: Unlike '모두', it shows a mood of people copying each other and crowding in all at once. It suits trends, popularity and rushes, and an action usually follows it.

examples.en: My room is so messy that I can't invite guests.
The top of your desk is really messy.
Clothes are scattered messily across the floor.

examples.ko: 너저분한 짐을 정리하느라 하루가 다 갔어요.
examples.en: I spent the whole day sorting out the cluttered stuff.
Even though I cleaned, the house is still untidy.
Put things back in place so it doesn't get messy.

explain: 물건이 여기저기 흩어져 어수선한 모습에 초점이 있어요. '지저분하다'는 더럽다는 뜻도 있지만, '너저분하다'는 정리가 안 된 느낌이 중심이에요.
explain_en: The focus is on things lying scattered around in disorder. '지저분하다' can also mean dirty, but '너저분하다' is mainly about things not being tidied up.

examples.en: I nailed a board over the window to block the wind.
It creaks when you walk on the old planks.
My father made a bookshelf out of boards.

examples.ko: 못 박은 널빤지가 떨어져 있어서 위험해요.
examples.en: A nailed board has come off, so it's dangerous.
This board is too short.
They put up a fence of boards in front of the construction site.

explain: 얇고 넓게 켠 나무 조각이에요. 비슷한 말로 '판자'가 있고, 일상에서는 '판자'를 더 짧게 말하기도 해요. 책꽂이나 울타리 같은 만들기 장면에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It is a thin, wide cut piece of wood. A similar word is '판자', which is shorter and also used in daily speech. It shows up in making things like bookshelves and fences.

examples.en: I hung the laundry out in the yard.
Hang the wet towels in the bathroom.
I've spread the chili peppers on the roof to dry them.

examples.ko: 비 오기 전에 널어놓은 이불을 걷어야 해요.
examples.en: I have to take in the bedding I hung out before it rains.
Don't leave your clothes lying around anywhere.
They spread all the toys across the living room and play.

explain: 말리려고 펴서 두는 모습이 기본이에요. 빨래는 '널다'가 더 짧고 흔하고, '널어놓다'는 그렇게 해 둔 상태를 강조해요. 장난감처럼 어질러 둘 때도 써요.
explain_en: The basic image is spreading something out to dry. For laundry '널다' is shorter and more common, while '널어놓다' emphasizes leaving it that way. It is also used for leaving things scattered, like toys.

examples.ko: 이 방은 널찍해서 가구를 놓기 좋아요.
examples.en: This room is spacious, so it's good for placing furniture.
It's convenient because there's a roomy parking lot.
The living room feels spacious.

examples.ko: 우리 좀 더 널찍한 집으로 이사 가요.
examples.en: Let's move to a somewhat roomier house.
Studying is more comfortable when the desk is roomy.
This cafe isn't spacious, but it's cozy.

explain: 그냥 '넓다'보다 공간에 여유가 있고 시원하다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 방, 마당, 자리처럼 공간을 말할 때 잘 써요.
explain_en: Compared to plain '넓다', it carries a pleasant feeling of room to spare and openness. It fits spaces such as rooms, yards and seats.

examples.en: I hurt my thigh while running.
My thigh muscles are knotted and sore.
The thigh part is the tastiest part of the chicken.
My thighs feel tight when I climb stairs.
I fell and got a bruise on my thigh.
Try doing thigh exercises regularly.

explain: 무릎 위쪽 다리 부분을 말하며 일상에서는 '허벅지'를 더 자주 말해요. 닭이나 돼지 요리 이야기에서도 나와요. 무릎 아래쪽은 '종아리'예요.
explain_en: It refers to the part of the leg above the knee, and in daily talk '허벅지' is heard more often. It also comes up when talking about chicken or pork dishes. The part below the knee is '종아리'.

examples.en: I received the keys on the day I paid the balance.

examples.ko: 공사 대금을 다 치른 뒤에야 열쇠를 넘겨받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only take over the keys after paying the full construction cost.
I took over the duties from my senior and am working on them.
I decided to take over my father's shop.
Once you receive the documents, please check them right away.

examples.ko: 새 담당자가 자료를 아직 넘겨받지 못했어요.
examples.en: The new person in charge hasn't received the materials yet.

explain: 반대말은 '넘겨주다'예요. 일, 재산, 서류, 열쇠처럼 책임이나 물건을 다른 사람에게서 이어받을 때 써요. 받는 사람이 주어이고, 사람에게는 '-에게서'를 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '넘겨주다' (to hand over). It is used when you take over responsibility or things like work, property, documents and keys from someone. The receiver is the subject, and the person you receive from takes '-에게서'.

examples.en: During the rainy season, the river overflows.
The bathtub overflowed and the floor got wet.
The market is overflowing with people's energy.

examples.ko: 눈물이 넘쳐흐를 것 같아서 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: I lowered my head because tears seemed about to spill over.
His words brimmed with confidence.
Be careful that the soup doesn't spill over.

explain: '넘치다'에 흘러내리는 느낌이 더해진 말이에요. 물뿐 아니라 활기, 자신감, 감정이 가득 차서 겉으로 드러날 때도 써요. '흐르다'가 '르 불규칙'이라서 '넘쳐흘러요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is '넘치다' with an added sense of flowing down. Besides water, it is used when energy, confidence or emotion is so full that it shows. Because '흐르다' is a '르' irregular verb, it becomes '넘쳐흘러요'.

examples.en: The pumpkin vine stretched long along the fence.
Cucumbers hung in clusters along the vine.

examples.ko: 할머니 집 벽이 넝쿨로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: The walls of my grandmother's house are covered with vines.
This vine grows taller every year.

examples.ko: 마당 한쪽에 포도 넝쿨 하나를 심었어요.
examples.en: I planted a grapevine in a corner of the yard.
Small flowers bloomed among the vines.

explain: 다른 것을 감거나 땅 위로 길게 뻗는 식물의 줄기를 말해요. '덩굴'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. '호박 넝쿨', '포도 넝쿨'처럼 식물 이름과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the long stem of a plant that climbs on things or creeps along the ground. '덩굴' is another word with the same meaning. It is used with plant names, as in '호박 넝쿨' and '포도 넝쿨'.

examples.ko: 친구 네댓 명이 우리 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: Four or five friends came to my house.
It'll probably take about four or five hours.
I bought four or five apples.

examples.ko: 아직 네댓 사람이 더 와야 해요.
examples.en: Four or five more people still need to come.

examples.ko: 이 일은 네댓 번 해 보면 익숙해져요.
examples.en: If you do this job four or five times, you get used to it.
You just go four or five stops by subway.

explain: 넷이나 다섯쯤이라는 대략의 수를 말해요. 뒤에 '명, 개, 번' 같은 단위 명사가 와요. 비슷하게 '두서너', '서너'처럼 어림수를 말하는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It gives a rough number of about four or five. A counter such as '명', '개' or '번' follows it. There are similar approximate-number words like '두서너' and '서너'.

examples.en: I put the gift in a neat square box.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 길이 네모반듯하게 나 있어요.
examples.en: The roads in our neighborhood are laid out in neat squares.
Please cut the paper into a neat square.
The window is a neat square, so it looks nice.

examples.ko: 그 건물은 네모반듯해서 좀 심심해 보여요.
examples.en: That building is boxy and looks a bit dull.
I folded the blanket into a neat square.

explain: 각이 잘 잡혀서 정돈된 네모 모양에 써요. 종이, 상자, 밭, 이불처럼 반듯하게 접거나 자른 것에 잘 어울려요. 단순히 '네모나다'보다 단정한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a tidy shape with well-formed square corners. It suits things folded or cut neatly, like paper, boxes, fields and blankets. It feels neater than simply '네모나다'.

examples.ko: 밤이 되자 거리의 네온사인이 하나둘 켜졌어요.
examples.en: When night fell, the neon signs on the street lit up one by one.
The neon sign in front of the shop keeps flickering.
I walked slowly under the glow of the neon signs.
Every building has flashy neon signs up.
There are many shops decorated with neon signs.
The glow of the neon signs was reflected on the wet street.

explain: 밤거리나 가게 간판을 말할 때 자주 나오는 외래어예요. 밤의 번화가 분위기를 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a loanword that often comes up when describing night streets and shop signs. It fits well when describing the atmosphere of a busy downtown at night.

examples.en: I tied the box up tightly with cord.
I bought a bundle of cord.
Tie the newspapers with cord and put them out.
The cord snapped and the load spilled out.
I hung the flowerpot up with cord.
Please cut the cord long.

explain: 짐이나 상자를 묶을 때 쓰는 꼬아 만든 가는 줄이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '끈'이나 '줄'이라고도 말해요. '노끈으로 묶다'가 가장 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
explain_en: It is a thin twisted rope used for tying up loads or boxes. In daily talk people also just say '끈' or '줄'. The most common usage is '노끈으로 묶다'.

examples.en: In old age, taking care of your health is the most important.
My grandfather spent his later years in the countryside.
Having a hobby in old age enriches your life.

examples.ko: 노년기가 길어져서 미리 준비하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Old age has become longer, so many people prepare in advance.

examples.ko: 그 화가는 노년기에 더욱 뛰어난 작품을 남겼어요.
examples.en: That painter left even better works in his later years.

examples.ko: 노년기의 외로움을 달래 주는 모임이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a group that soothes the loneliness of old age.

explain: '청년기', '중년기'처럼 인생을 나눈 시기의 하나예요. 일상 대화에서는 '노후'나 '나이 들어서'라고 더 자주 말하고, '노년기'는 설명하는 글이나 수업에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is one of the life stages like '청년기' and '중년기'. In daily conversation people more often say '노후' or '나이 들어서', while '노년기' appears mostly in explanatory writing and lessons.

examples.en: We have to protect workers' labor rights.
Part-time workers must also have their labor rights guaranteed.

examples.ko: 학교에서도 노동권 교육을 해야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think schools should teach about labor rights too.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원의 노동권을 무시해서 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That company ignored its employees' labor rights and became a problem.
Where should I report it if my labor rights are violated?
I saw a rally on the news calling for protecting labor rights.

explain: 뉴스와 사회 수업에서 '노동권을 보장하다', '노동권을 침해하다', '노동권을 보호하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 일하는 사람이 가지는 권리를 두루 가리킬 때 써요.
explain_en: It appears often in news and social studies as '노동권을 보장하다', '노동권을 침해하다' and '노동권을 보호하다'. It is used broadly for the rights that working people have.

examples.ko: 요즘 노동량이 너무 많아서 쉴 틈이 없어요.
examples.en: My workload is so heavy these days that I have no time to rest.
Would efficiency go up if we reduced the daily workload?
The pay is the same, but the workload is double.
The pay is low compared to the amount of work.

examples.ko: 이 일은 노동량이 많은 대신 월급이 높아요.
examples.en: This job has a lot of labor, but in return the pay is high.
We decided to split the workload among the team members.

explain: 일하는 데 드는 일의 양을 말하고, '노동량이 많다/적다', '노동량을 줄이다'처럼 써요. 사무직 일에는 '업무량'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is about how much work a job requires, used as '노동량이 많다/적다' and '노동량을 줄이다'. For office work people also say '업무량'.
